alloys.alloys_notes: Nominal composition Fe-30Mn-9Al-1C-1V-5Ni (wt.%). Measured ingot composition (Table 1, wt.%) differs slightly: Mn 30.45, Al 9.50, C 1.20, V 1.09, Ni 4.94, P 0.0040, S 0.0044, Fe Bal. Fe, Mn, Al, Ni, V analyzed by ICP-OES and C by combustion-infrared absorption.
alloys.description: A high-Mn Fe-Mn-Al-C lightweight steel designed to form an austenite-B2 dual-phase heterogeneous structure with dual-nanoprecipitation (L'12-type LRO domains and VC carbides) within austenite, aiming at simultaneous ultrahigh strength and ductility. Prepared via induction melting under high-purity argon.

source.reason: Abstract and Introduction explicitly state the designed composition 'Fe-30Mn-9Al-1C-1V-5Ni (wt.%)', and Materials and Methods give the nominal composition of the 10 kg ingot with Table 1 listing measured compositions. This is the single alloy system studied in the paper.

paper.paper_scope: Design an Fe-30Mn-9Al-1C-1V-5Ni (wt.%) austenite-B2 duplex lightweight steel processed by cold rolling and heat treatment, and investigate its microstructure, mechanical properties, strengthening mechanisms and deformation behavior to achieve ultrahigh strength-ductility synergy.
paper.title: An Ultrastrong and Ductile Duplex Lightweight Steel with Dual-Nanoprecipitation

processes.description: Plates first homogenized at 1050 °C for 1 h, then hot-rolled to 3 mm thickness and immediately water-quenched to room temperature; subsequently cold-rolled to ~1.5 mm (single-pass reduction ≤5%, total thickness reduction 50%); finally solution-treated at 900 °C for 15 min followed by water quenching, giving the austenite + B2 duplex microstructure with VC and L'12 LRO nanoprecipitates.
processes.process_name: Homogenization + hot rolling + water quenching + cold rolling (50%) + solution treatment 900 °C/15 min + water quenching
processes.processes_notes: The paper describes a single processing route; subsequent tensile/in-situ deformation states (0%, 1%, 3%, 6%, 12% strain) are test conditions of this same solution-treated material rather than separate processes.

source.reason: Materials and Methods (b0025) fully specify the thermomechanical route: homogenization at 1050 °C/1 h, hot rolling to 3 mm with water quenching, cold rolling to ~1.5 mm (50% total reduction), then solution treatment at 900 °C for 15 min with water quenching (Figure 1a). This defines the terminal state of the studied material.

The only material studied is the Fe-30Mn-9Al-1C-1V-5Ni (wt.%) duplex lightweight steel subjected to the single rolling + heat treatment route described in Materials and Methods; the alloy and process uniquely define this sample.

unmapped_findings: The duplex lightweight steel's microstructure comprises austenite and B2 phases with a B2 phase volume fraction of ~20% (XRD), average austenite grain size 1.31 µm, bimodal B2 grain sizes 1.02 µm and 3.38 µm.
Dual-nanoprecipitation: L'12-type LRO domains in austenite have average size 1.0 ± 0.3 nm and volume fraction 11.10%; VC precipitates have average size 19.9 ± 6.2 nm and volume fraction 0.26%.
Mechanical properties: YS = 1316 ± 16 MPa, UTS = 1458 ± 11 MPa, total elongation = 11.7 ± 1.2%, with three work-hardening stages and work-hardening rate remaining 2.7–3.7 GPa in stage III.

Strengthening mechanism contributions: σ0,γ = 97 MPa, σ0,B2 = 676 MPa, solid solution σSS,γ = 228 MPa, dislocation forest σdis = 106 MPa (austenite) and 227 MPa (B2), VC Orowan σVC = 92 MPa, HDI σHDI = 597 MPa, LRO σLRO ≈ 119 MPa.
